correctness.rationale: For every b≥2,r≥1, base-ell finite subset sums are distinct in (0,1/2) and yield irrational, distinct b-power mantissas, by their nonintegral q-adic exponent for some q|b. Open level-K digit cylinders separate all 2^r−1 subset products. A common perturbation radius preserves separation, so primes chosen from fixed proportional intervals yield all nonunit divisor words with pairwise different first K base-b digits and therefore prefix-free. The PNT gives ≫(b^L/L)^r distinct products per scale; choosing L=floor(log_b(X/C)/r) proves ≫X/(log X)^r. All constraints, r=1, bases with perfect powers, and arbitrary large X are handled. Explicit finite verifier checks examples but is not used as infinite proof.
